_meta.description: Per-layer ambient tint for the world. Applied by src/world/LayerVisuals.gd to TerrainManager.tile_map.modulate — the TERRAIN TileMap and nothing else.
_meta.status: FIRST-PASS VISUAL VALUES — pending an art pass. These are VISUAL values, not balance values; they do not belong to the balance pass and are tuned by eye.
_meta._first_pass: 2026-07-30 first-pass visual values. Rebuilt from scratch after the original file was lost to a git clean.
_meta._scope_note: Deliberately NOT a CanvasModulate. A scene-wide CanvasModulate multiplies every canvas item — player, TestDummies, LootDrop gems and the Main.gd background gradient included — which muddies them all with the ambient colour and collapses figure/ground readability. Tinting only the TileMap gives the same ambient read while every actor, item and the backdrop stay true-colour for free.
_meta._range_note: These are MULTIPLIED onto the terrain art, so every channel stays roughly in 0.75-1.0. Anything heavier crushes the tile art's own detail and hue. Each layer also keeps its brightest channel at or near 1.0 so the tint reads as a hue shift, not as dimming — depth darkening is already handled separately by DepthHazard's screen-space vignette, and doubling up would black out the terrain.
_meta._null_rule: Any layer that is absent, null, or missing/non-numeric r/g/b leaves the terrain at Color.WHITE (no tint). LayerVisuals never invents a colour.

_transition_note: Seconds to cross-fade the terrain tint on a layer change. Short enough to land while the player is still near the boundary, long enough not to pop. 0 = snap instantly. LayerVisuals falls back to 1.2 only if this key is absent or null.

ambient_tint._note: r/g/b in 0.0-1.0. Alpha is intentionally not configurable — a translucent TileMap would show the backdrop gradient through solid rock.
